resources.string: No computer needed on supported devices. Enable Developer options (press Android TV OS build seven times in Settings → System → About), then USB debugging. The app needs local ADB on port 5555; Wireless debugging pairing alone is not enough.
2. Authorize local ADB and allow restricted settings

The app will connect to this TV only and ask Android to allow restricted settings for Android VideoInfoOverlay. It will not enable Accessibility for you or change other accessibility services.\n\nAccept the TV’s “Allow USB debugging?” prompt. Choose “Always allow” to let the overlay reconnect for playback metrics. ADB gives this app powerful shell access; continue only if you trust it. Leave debugging enabled only on a trusted network.
Local ADB permission has not been checked in this session.
Connecting locally… Watch for “Allow USB debugging?” on the TV and accept. Waiting up to 60 seconds for approval.
Restricted settings allowed and verified. Enable Accessibility below, then press Back to return here.
Setup did not complete: %1$s\nCheck USB debugging and port 5555, then retry. If this device does not expose local ADB, computer-assisted setup may still be required.
Accessibility service not connected yet. Enable Android VideoInfoOverlay in Accessibility, then return here. Other services can remain enabled.
Accessibility service connected. Ready to show the overlay.
This settings shortcut is unavailable. Open the corresponding screen from the TV’s Settings app, then return here.
